title: Advice Administrator
description:
Job Title: Advice Administrator

Job Description

We are seeking a proactive, customer-focused Advice Administrator to provide practical advice and support to customers, particularly those in vulnerable circumstances. The role involves working from a mobile advice van, attending community events, providing telephone and face-to-face support, and completing administrative duties.

The successful candidate will assess customer needs, provide tailored guidance, identify eligibility for funding and financial assistance, and refer customers to relevant support services. They will also maintain accurate records, contribute to reporting, build relationships with partner organisations and help improve service delivery.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide high-quality, tailored advice and support to customers.
- Conduct customer assessments and identify appropriate support and funding opportunities.
- Deliver telephone and face-to-face advice, including support for vulnerable customers.
- Maintain accurate customer records and update CRM systems.
- Complete administrative tasks and assist with reporting.
- Meet agreed KPIs and contribute to overall project targets.
- Attend community events and develop relationships with partner organisations.
- Identify opportunities to improve processes and customer service.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues to ensure effective service delivery.

Essential Requirements
- Full, valid UK driving licence and access to a vehicle for business use.
- Appropriate business insurance, with eligible mileage expenses reimbursed.
- Ability to drive a large commercial van.
- Basic DBS check.
- Excellent communication, customer service and organisational skills.
- Strong IT skills, including CRM systems and Microsoft Office.
- Ability to manage workloads, meet targets and maintain accurate records.
- Empathy and a commitment to supporting vulnerable customers.

Previous experience in customer service, advice provision or administration is desirable. Candidates must be proactive, adaptable and able to work independently and as part of a team.

title: Bookkeeper
description:
We are currently recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Bookkeeper / Legal Cashier to join their team.

Our client is looking to attract candidates with experience across bookkeeping, general accounts or legal cashiering, with opportunities available for individuals at varying levels of experience.

Whether you have a general accounts background or specialist experience managing client and office accounts within a legal practice, we would be keen to hear from you.

The Role

Depending on your experience and background, responsibilities may include:
- Managing the day-to-day bookkeeping and accounts function.
- Maintaining accurate and up-to-date financial records.
- Processing purchase and sales invoices, payments and receipts.
- Completing regular bank reconciliations.
- Managing supplier payments and customer transactions.
- Assisting with VAT returns and general financial administration.
- Managing client and office accounts within a legal practice.
- Processing legal account transactions, transfers and payments.
- Ensuring compliance with relevant financial procedures and SRA Accounts Rules.
- Handling more complex transactions and working independently where required.

About You

We are interested in hearing from candidates with experience in one or more of the following areas:
- Previous bookkeeping or general accounts experience.
- Experience working within a legal practice or law firm's accounts department.
- Knowledge of client and office accounts.
- Understanding of SRA Accounts Rules.
- Strong reconciliation and financial administration skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills.
- The ability to manage workloads independently and meet deadlines.

title: Corporate Services Administrator
description:
Corporate Services Administrator

Halifax

£30,000 - £37,000

NJR Recruitment is currently working with a well-established financial services business that is looking to recruit an experienced Corporate Services Administrator to join its growing team.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a background in Employee Benefits or Corporate Financial Services who has hands-on experience supporting Group Risk and Private Medical Insurance (PMI) schemes.

Working as part of a dedicated Corporate Services team, you will provide comprehensive administrative support to corporate clients, advisers and colleagues, ensuring a professional, efficient and compliant service.

The Role

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing day-to-day administration support for corporate employee benefit schemes.
- Managing Group Risk arrangements, including Group Life Assurance and Group Income Protection.
- Administering Private Medical Insurance (PMI) schemes and cash plans.
- Handling renewals, rebroking exercises and obtaining quotations from providers.
- Processing claims and checking provider accounts.
- Preparing documentation and meeting packs for advisers.
- Following up on adviser meeting actions and ensuring all tasks are completed.
- Supporting workplace pension schemes, including processing contributions.
- Assisting corporate clients with Auto-Enrolment, re-declarations and salary exchange queries.
- Maintaining accurate client records and ensuring all documentation meets compliance requirements.
- Building strong working relationships with clients, providers, advisers and colleagues.

About You

To be considered for this opportunity, you will ideally have:
- Previous experience working within Employee Benefits, Corporate Services or Group Risk administration.
- Essential: Hands-on experience administering Group Risk schemes, including Group Life and/or Group Income Protection.
- Essential: Previous experience administering Private Medical Insurance (PMI) schemes.
- Experience dealing with renewals, rebroking and provider liaison.
- A good understanding of workplace pensions and employee benefits.
- Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail.
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and work to deadlines.
- A professional and client-focused approach.
- An understanding of FCA regulations, compliance and Consumer Duty.
- A relevant industry qualification, or a willingness to work towards one.

What's on Offer?
- The opportunity to join an established and professional financial services business.
- A varied role covering a broad range of corporate employee benefits.
- The opportunity to develop your knowledge and industry qualifications.
- A supportive team environment.

Interested?

If you have experience across Group Risk and PMI administration and are looking for your next career move, we'd love to hear from you.

Contact NJR Recruitment today quoting NJR17104 for a confidential discussion.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller -Fixed Term Contract

We are looking for an experienced and motivated Credit Controller to join a growing business near Halifax area for a 6 month fixed term contract.

You'll take ownership of your own customer portfolio, focusing on maximising cash collection, reducing aged debt and building strong customer relationships. This is a fast-paced, hands-on role suited to someone who enjoys a challenge, is confident on the phone and thrives working towards targets.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage a portfolio of customer accounts, proactively chasing outstanding payments.
- Reduce aged debt and maximise cash collection.
- Make regular outbound calls to negotiate payments and resolve outstanding balances.
- Log invoice queries and work with internal teams to ensure timely resolution.
- Record payment promises and support cash flow forecasting.
- Build strong customer relationships to encourage timely payments.
- Identify and escalate high-risk or unrecoverable debts.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues to improve processes and performance.

About You
- Previous experience in Credit Control or Accounts Receivable.
- Confident making outbound calls and negotiating payments.
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
- Able to manage your own workload and prioritise effectively.
- Target-driven, proactive and commercially aware.
- A positive team player with a continuous improvement mindset.

This role will be full time working Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM, with excellent hybrid working to be offered.

Interested?

If you're an experienced Credit Controller looking for your next challenge within a growing and supportive team and want to know more details, we'd love to hear from you!

Apply today!

Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age

title: Finance and Payroll Assistant
description:
?A fantastic organisation based in the Halifax area are recruiting a part time (3/4 days per week) Finance & Payroll Assistant to join their small finance team. Reporting directly to the FD you will get involved in the smooth processing of c 130 staff members weekly payroll along with other area of wider finance.

Duties & Responsibilities:
- Process payroll on a weekly basis by extracting information from the timesheet system, reformatting as required, checking and uploading into the payroll software. Calculate adjustments around sick pay, holiday pay, parental leave, etc.
- Perform payroll checks with the support of the payroll officer ensuring payroll is delivered in a timely manner and relevant information is provided to enable it to be paid through the bank on time.
- Maintain appropriate payroll records so that queries can be answered promptly and accounting records are kept up to date.
- Process all sales ledger invoices in the month for the relevant business areas and ensure they're sent out in a timely manner, debts are collected and chased. Any queries are dealt with promptly.
- Process all purchase ledger invoices in the month, ensuring timely payment and approvals.
- Monitor the bank to ensure funds are in the correct place on a regular basis.
- Post journals into the accounting system for month end on a timely basis. Prepare and post accruals and prepayments as required with support from the wider finance team.
- Assist with preparing simple management accounts analysing against budget.
- Support the wider Finance team at as required.
- Any other ad hoc tasks as required.

We would be keen to hear from candidates with the following skills and experience:
- Previous weekly payroll processing experience
- Experience in wider finance including all elements of transactional finance / Assistant Accounting
- To work confidently as part of a team
- Have a flexible attitude to work and have a hands-on approach
- Have a professional attitude to your work.
- If you are looking

Sharp Consultancy is a finance and accountancy recruitment specialist assisting accounting and finance divisions of businesses in the Yorkshire and Derbyshire area. With over 30 years' experience we pride ourselves on sourcing excellent finance professionals across all divisions of an accounts function.

Candidates must be eligible to work in the UK full time without restriction. To apply please send your CV to the e-mail address stated, quoting our reference and specifying which website you saw this position advertised on. Due to the high volume of applications, we receive it is not always possible to respond to unsuccessful applicants. Therefore, if we have not responded to your application within seven days, please note that on this occasion your application has not been successful.

title: Load Planner
description:
Job Specification: Load Planner

Department / Location: Transport, Halifax
Reports To: Transport Manager
People Responsibility: Drivers and Mates

Main Purpose

To manage day-to-day transport operations, including driver allocation, route planning and transport administration, ensuring customer service requirements are met efficiently and within budget.

Key Responsibilities
- Allocate work to drivers and mates to maximise vehicle utilisation and workforce efficiency, monitoring performance and taking corrective action where necessary.
- Ensure drivers and mates follow company Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and established working practices.
- Plan daily delivery routes using Paragon, ensuring the appropriate vehicles are deployed to meet customer requirements while minimising costs.
- Ensure loads remain within vehicle payload limits and comply with drivers' hours regulations.
- Ensure drivers and mates receive appropriate inductions and training, maintaining accurate records and identifying further training needs.
- Ensure vehicles and associated equipment are operated safely and in accordance with current legislation and company policies.
- Produce transport performance reports and KPIs accurately and on time for internal and external use.
- Ensure compliance with Health and Safety and fire safety regulations, including the correct use of company uniforms and personal protective equipment (PPE).
- Complete order processing and prepare pick lists, despatch notes and load sheets in accordance with depot procedures.
- Provide support to warehouse management when required.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
- On-time delivery performance.
- Vehicle fill rates and payload utilisation.
- Delivery cost per drop.
- Driver compliance, including drivers' hours and vehicle walk-round checks.
- Completion of training and up-to-date induction records.

Key Working Relationships

Internal
- Transport Manager
- Warehouse Team
- Customer Service Team
- Fleet and Maintenance Team

External
- Customers
- Hauliers and third-party carriers
- Paragon system support

Qualifications, Skills and Experience
- Previous experience in transport planning, ideally using Paragon.
- Working knowledge of drivers' hours regulations and operator licence requirements.
- Strong IT, organisational and communication skills.
- Ability to work under pressure and meet daily delivery deadlines.
- Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
- Ability to work effectively with drivers, warehouse teams and other departments.
- A proactive approach to improving transport efficiency and customer service.

title: Administrator
description: The Administrator plays a vital role in ensuring the smooth and efficient running of Northpoint Calderdale services. Working as part of a small, friendly, and supportive administrative team, the post holder will provide essential administrative support across all areas of the service. The Administrator will be the first point of contact for clients, families and professionals accessing Northpoint mental health and wellbeing support by phone, email or in person. They will support day to day service operations through accurate record keeping and scheduling. They will also provide reception and facilities support, maintaining a welcoming, well-organised office and helping to create a professional, inclusive and safe environment for staff and visitors. Duties and Responsibilities Receive and process referrals, support appointment booking and rearrangements, and manage related communications with stakeholders, including professionals, families and young people. Respond to email and telephone enquiries, including those from external professionals, ensuring accurate and timely information sharing. Manage, allocate, and input client and professional referrals as required, ensuring accuracy and confidentiality in data management. Oversee client referral inboxes and provide administrative support for ongoing service monitoring and reporting. Monitor the quality of data and liaise with the information gathering team and practitioners to support accurate record keeping and service delivery. Prepare rooms for use and carry out daily opening and closing checks. Undertake general housekeeping tasks, including maintaining the coffee machine and operating the dishwasher. Assist with ordering and maintaining stationery, supplies, and small equipment, and support facilities tasks that keep the office safe, tidy, and well-equipped. Help facilitate internal and external events, meetings, and training sessions, including arranging refreshments. Manage the room booking system and provide support to new users. Provide administrative support to managers and colleagues, including preparing correspondence and organising meetings or events. Provide a warm, professional, and inclusive welcome to clients, families, and visitors accessing the service in person or over the phone. Maintain a calm, welcoming reception space with up to date information and clear communication on health, safety, and wellbeing. Do you want to be part of the difference we’re making to mental health and wellbeing across our communities? Are you an organised and approachable administrator who takes pride in keeping things running smoothly and creating a welcoming environment for others? This is a great opportunity to join Northpoint as an Administrator within our Calderdale services. You’ll play a key role in supporting the day-to-day running of our busy Halifax office, helping ensure that children, young people, families and professionals receive a responsive and well-organised service. You will join us on a full-time*, permanent basis (35 hours per week) with a FTE salary of £26,240 – £28,470 . *Please note, part-time hours of 28+ will also be considered. Why us? Northpoint is a leading regional provider of mental health services for children, young people and adults across Yorkshire. We work in partnership with local services to deliver accessible, high-quality support that meets people’s needs at the right time. At Northpoint, you’ll be part of a supportive, collaborative organisation where your contribution matters. We offer: 35-hour full time working week Flexible working arrangements* 238 hours annual leave (including Bank holidays) plus statutory holidays pro rata and up to 3 discretionary leave days at Christmas. Auto-enrolment pension scheme Enhanced leave policies that support you when it matters most Regular supervision and development opportunities A supportive, inclusive and values-led working environment *Please note - this is an office-based role at our Halifax premises, due to the nature of the work and the need for regular in-person support. What you will be doing as our Administrator As an Administrator, you will be a key part of a small and friendly team, supporting the smooth and efficient running of services and acting as a first point of contact for those accessing support. You will be responsible for: Acting as a first point of contact for clients, families and professionals, both in person and via phone/email Managing and processing referrals, including booking and rearranging appointments Monitoring and maintaining inboxes, ensuring timely and accurate responses Recording and maintaining accurate, confidential data and client records Supporting reporting, data quality and service monitoring Providing reception and front-of-house support, ensuring a welcoming and professional environment Managing room bookings and supporting meetings, events and training sessions Supporting general office and facilities tasks, including maintaining supplies and shared spaces Providing administrative support to managers and colleagues across the service What are we looking for in our ideal Administrator? We’re looking for someone who is organised, reliable and enjoys working in a varied, people-facing role. You will bring: Experience in an administrative or office support role Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities Excellent attention to detail and accuracy Confident communication skills, both written and verbal Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office systems Understanding of confidentiality and data protection principles A proactive, flexible and solution-focused approach Ability to work both independently and as part of a team A friendly, professional approach when working with clients and colleagues Experience in a health, education, or charity setting would be beneficial but is not essential. This is a varied and rewarding role where you’ll make a real difference by supporting the delivery of mental health services and helping people access the support they need. If you take pride in keeping things organised and want to work in a role where your contribution really matters, we’d love to hear from you. Interested? Please click ‘ Apply ’ to be considered for our Administrator role. Closing date: Sunday 06 December 2026 Provisional Interview Date: Thursday 17 December 2026 We may use digital interviews as part of the recruitment process. We aim to be a talented, resilient and inclusive community. We welcome applications from all and offer flexible working opportunities where possible. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults, and expect all staff to share this commitment. This post is subject to an Enhanced DBS check. It's important to us that our recruitment process is inclusive and person-centred. If you require any support or adjustments to access any stage of the recruitment process, please contact our Recruitment Team at recruitment@northpoint.org.uk to discuss how we can support you.
